name: AWS Firecracker
version_context: MicroVM design for multi-tenant cloud workloads
summary: A minimal virtual machine monitor that combines hardware virtualization isolation with a deliberately small device model and fast lifecycle operations.

features.name: Minimal machine model
features.description: A Firecracker process encapsulates one microVM and exposes a deliberately limited set of emulated and paravirtualized devices.
benefits: Reduces device-model complexity and attack surface
costs: Provides less general hardware compatibility than a full VMM

features.name: KVM-backed event-driven VMM
features.description: Guest CPU execution uses KVM while device emulation and control work are organized around dedicated threads and an epoll-based event loop.
benefits: Supports fast lifecycle operations and high resource density
costs: Correctness and performance depend on carefully coordinating host, VMM, and guest execution

mathematical_views.question: How can a system combine VM isolation with a smaller operational and device surface?
assumptions: KVM provides the modeled hardware isolation boundary
The reduced device model is sufficient for the target workloads

mathematical_views.question: How do API commands, VMM events, and virtual CPU execution evolve one microVM state?
assumptions: Each command has defined preconditions and state effects
Resource limits are part of the transition semantics

benefits: Smaller trusted computing base and faster startup path
costs: Reduced compatibility with workloads requiring a broad virtual hardware surface

benefits: Efficient execution of many small virtual machines
costs: More specialized scheduling and I/O assumptions

evidence.title: Firecracker Design
evidence.notes: Primary design documentation for the VMM architecture and threading model.

relations.notes: Both are virtual machine monitors, but Firecracker deliberately narrows the device model while QEMU provides broad machine and device emulation; this is a structural comparison, not reuse or equivalence.
